R1A-bear-backcountry-0004.name: 1.6 km N of Turret Mountain
R1A-bear-backcountry-0004.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R1A-bear-backcountry-0004.parkWhat: pull off on Effingham Ml East (paved road)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2014 (12 years old), 300 m N: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
S facing slope, 10 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 120 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

Park: 49.13007, -125.22677, pull off on Effingham Ml East (paved road). Map links below.
Walk: 5.1 km SE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 750 m, about 177 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 140 m SW of the spot at 8 m (49.09161, -125.18833). Water: unnamed wetland 170 m E (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov, Dec (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 1-8, Region 1. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
